title: Provider
description: Learn how to make the Redux store available to React components.

data.text: **Provider** is the bridge between Redux and React. It wraps your entire application and makes the Redux `store` available to every component that needs it. Without Provider, components would have no way to access the store.

Provider uses React's **Context API** internally. When you wrap your app with Provider, it creates a context that holds the Redux store. Any component can then access this store using hooks like `useSelector` and `useDispatch`.

data.text: While most applications use a single store, you can create multiple stores using separate contexts. This is rare but useful for large applications that need completely isolated state trees.

cards.title: Single Store
cards.content: Most applications use one store. All state lives in one place, making debugging easier. Best for apps under 50 components.

cards.title: Multiple Stores
cards.content: Create separate contexts with `createContext()`. Use when you need completely isolated state (e.g., multi-tenant apps). More complex to set up.

data.content: Using separate contexts for multiple stores

data.title: Store Instance Warning
data.text: Never create the store inside a component body. This causes a new store on every render, breaking state persistence.

data.title: Set Up Provider in Your App
data.description: Create a new React app with Redux and set up the Provider component. Make sure the store is defined outside the component to prevent recreation on each render.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Provider makes the Redux store available to all React components
It uses React's Context API internally
Wrap your root component to give all children access to the store
Define the store outside components to prevent recreation
Multiple stores are possible using separate contexts (rare use case)
data.takeaway: Provider is the essential bridge that connects Redux to React, enabling the hooks API for state management.
